title: Emerging Technology Weekly Briefing
description: Quantum and post-quantum cryptography, robotics and autonomy, advanced compute, and space-enabled tech.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 26–Nov. 3. No new post-quantum standard, Army quantum award, autonomy test, or space-delivery result dated Nov. 2–3 was found. The newest item remains Tom's Hardware's Nov. 1 report on the Air Force Research Lab's Starfall cargo recovery. PsiQuantum's Oct. 30 optical-switch demo is on the data-center page. The compute subsection is empty.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Air Force Research Lab recovered SpaceX Starfall cargo pods in the Pacific
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 1 that the Air Force Research Lab recovered agile cargo pods after a SpaceX Starfall capsule splashed down in the Pacific. Tom's Hardware says the pods launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on a Falcon 9 as part of the Bandwagon-5 rideshare, and that an Air Force Research Lab post on Oct. 26 said each pod carried representative mission equipment, including meals ready to eat, bottled water, a SATCOM-enabled tracker, and spare batteries, so the lab could study temperature, shock, and vibration. Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly called the recovery a demonstration of Rocket Cargo point-to-point delivery. Tom's Hardware says the Starfall capsule is about 10 feet across and has a capacity of up to 2,200 pounds.

items.headline: AWS Key Management Service adds ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation
items.summary: AWS said Oct. 26 that Key Management Service now supports Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism, ML-KEM, which it identifies as the NIST FIPS 203 standard meant to replace Diffie-Hellman, elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman and RSA key transport. AWS says the point is the harvest-now, decrypt-later risk, in which an adversary records a key exchange today and recovers it once a quantum computer can. KMS supports ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024. AWS says the private key stays in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware security modules, and that the feature is available in every KMS region except the Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain) and China regions.

items.headline: Google Cloud puts Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 in public preview
items.summary: Google Cloud said Oct. 27 that Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is in public preview on the Gemini platform. Google describes it as a model that works across robot bodies, from stationary arms to humanoids, and that combines spatial and temporal video understanding with long-horizon planning and safety guardrails. Google says developers can declare low-level controls, including vision-language-action models and navigation APIs, as tools, and can test behaviors in MuJoCo-Warp and NVIDIA Isaac Sim before using hardware. Boston Dynamics' Marco da Silva said the model changes what an inspection with Spot can be, because applying models to video lets the robot do more than check a single moment.
